rationale: M59 (#825). Every line below is read off declaration-lines-825.java. An annotation is a modifier, so a declaration's line is where the declaration is written: `@SuppressWarnings("unused")` on 20 must not become the line of `Annotated` (21), `@Deprecated` on 23 must not become the line of `legacy` (24), and `@Override` on 26 must not become the line of the overriding `label` (27). Measured on a 300-file real java sample: 25 of 93 symbols landed on an annotation before this contract, so a tool navigating to a java symbol opened `@SuppressWarnings` instead of the class. Also pinned: each parent of a multi-line heritage list is named on its OWN line (`extends Base` on 21, `implements Marker, Serializable` on 22), containment points at the member's declaration, and an override points at the overriding declaration rather than at its annotation. The forbid entries are the pre-fix positions.

forbidRelationships.note: pre-fix: the `@Deprecated` line; `int legacy = 1;` is written on 24
pre-fix: the `@Override` line; the overriding method is written on 27
pre-fix: the override was attributed to the annotation line
